profile.headline: Software Engineer
profile.summary:
I am a web developer based in Richmond, Virginia with strong roots in my local game development community. My career has been focused on fullstack AWS cloud based solutions, relying on backends comprised of Node.Js lambdas and frontends built with some kind of SPA framework like React or Angular.

I got my start in a fintech startup and now currently work on building complete custom applications for public sector organizations.

I'll always take Typescript over vanilla Javascript.

I'm a fan of unit testing, even if it's just for my own development process and no routine automated testing is ever setup.

You should probably just use a relational database unless you have a very clear specific reason for using a NOSQL solution. Even then, it's usually better to wait to iterate into a NOSQL solution once you're certain you actually have the problem it solves rather than start with one.

Happy to learn whatever tools are needed for the job.

More interested in solving customers' problems than tech for its own sake.

More interested in figuring out how to represent requirements with code than tools.

I can navigate a codebase built on AWS but you don't want me setting up your infrastructure.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Building custom applications for public sector organizations.

I worked on several small teams helping build custom applications for public sector organizations in a full stack capacity. Our frontends were built with React, Zustand and Material UI. The backends made heavy use of AWS services, making extensive use of Cognito, Parameter Store, DynamoDB, Cloudwatch, S3, Cloudformation, Lambdas and Codepipeline.

I piloted the use of DynamoDB at the company and I was the pilot user for a lot of our internally developed tools on projects. I also worked on projects making use of event sourcing, event driven architecture and GQL based graph services. I was part of pushes to embrace unit testing ( Jest ) and Typescript in the company, experimenting with Test Driven Development (TDD) and pair programming.

I also got to enjoy the novelty of integrating a barcode scanner on an application.

 My current project relies on Nest.js.
positions.insights: React.js, Amazon Web Services (AWS) and +3 skills

positions.title: Junior Javascript Fullstack Engineer
positions.description:
A broker dealer and fintech company, Wealthforge is building the premier online platform for
alternative investments, Altigo. Altigo automated the laborious process behind investing in
many alternative investment products, such as Delaware Statutory Trusts (DSTs) and Real
Estate Investment Trusts (REITs), turning a traditionally error-prone, months long process into
something that could be conveniently handled in a matter of days with consistent success.

My Responsibilities:
- Fixed bugs and added features to Altigo’s Angular UI
- Setup resolvers in an Apollo server to help support new tables added to the database.
- Wrote GQL queries against our Hasura graph service and codegen’d services for them
to add new functionality and analyze the database.
- Altered code in AWS Node.js lambdas to fix bugs and alter functionality to suit customer
needs directly. A substantial project I worked on was getting a bespoke CSV export set
up for an individual customer according to their specific needs that ran routinely
according to a CRON job.
- Added features, fixed bugs and added support for new kinds of data in our Altigo Admin
tool built with Ruby on Rails and Rails Admin. Picked up the Ruby programming
language and the Ruby on Rails and Rails Admin frameworks in a week so I could lend
support for a tool where we had few programmers with the skills necessary to work on it.
- Contributed in design discussions around how to address requirements across the
database, admin tool and Altigo UI. Collaborated frequently with our DBA on how to
design the tables to support new requirements.
- Attended calls with clients as the developer that would be directly addressing the
functionality they are looking for. Also participated in production support calls when an
extra set of eyes was requested to help solve tricky issues.
- Wrote documentation on matters such as how to run our lambdas locally and how to
create new user roles in AWS’s IAM system
positions.insights: Ruby on Rails, Hasura and +15 skills
